findings.location: content.body.ruleUk: "Haber + дієприкметник (-ado, -ido) — завершену дію: He comido."; content.body.scope.noteUk: "З estar — герундій (-ando, -iendo), з haber — дієприкметник (-ado, -ido)."
findings.description: Completion is presented as a general meaning of haber + participle, although perfect constructions allow continuing situations, as in He vivido aquí desde niño. The categorical auxiliary rule also excludes grammatical resultative estar + participle, such as estar cenado.
findings.suggestion: Describe the progressive and perfect constructions explicitly. Limit the completed-event explanation to He comido, and avoid implying that estar cannot combine with a participle.

items.reviewerAnswer: Estoy comiendo describes eating in progress; he comido reports prior eating. Perfect constructions do not invariably imply that a situation has ended, and estar can also take resultative participles.
sources: RAE/ASALE, Nueva gramática de la lengua española, chapter 23, pretérito perfecto compuesto and continuative interpretations (from memory).
RAE/ASALE, Nueva gramática de la lengua española, chapter 27, adjectival and predicative uses of participles (from memory).

findings.location: task.prompt[1].text: "Ahora mis padres están ___ (cenar)."; task.accepted contains only "cenando" with task.closed set to true.
findings.description: The prompt does not distinguish an ongoing action from a resulting state. Están cenando means they are eating dinner; están cenados means they have had dinner. The instruction permits either a gerund or a participle, but the closed key covers only the progressive reading.
findings.suggestion: Specify whether the parents are currently eating or have already eaten before finalizing the key; alternatively, accept and explain both readings.

items.reviewerAnswer: cenando for an ongoing dinner; cenados for the resulting state of having eaten dinner. Both fit the wording.
items.notes: Ahora does not by itself exclude a resulting state.
sources: RAE/ASALE, Diccionario de la lengua española, entry cenado, da, adjectival meaning referring to someone who has eaten dinner (from memory).
Course contract, rule 3; verdict definition for uncertain cases with multiple reasonable readings.

findings.location: task.prompt[1].text: "Ahora Luis está ___ en la cocina."; task.options[1] labels "comido" incorrect and says "Після está — герундій: está comiendo."
findings.description: Está comido can describe someone who has eaten, a resultative use available in Spain Spanish. Neither Ahora nor en la cocina establishes that Luis is currently eating. The key and feedback assume the progressive reading without specifying it.
findings.suggestion: Add context explicitly placing Luis in the middle of eating, or allow both options with explanations of their different meanings.

items.reviewerAnswer: a for ongoing eating; b for the resulting state of having eaten. Both readings are possible.
sources: RAE/ASALE, Diccionario de la lengua española, entry comido, da, adjectival meaning referring to someone who has eaten (from memory).
Course contract, rule 2; verdict definition for uncertain cases with multiple reasonable readings.
